title: create --dry-run plans a changeset without writing it, on both spellings
expectation: `monochange create --dry-run` and `monochange step create-change-file --dry-run` exit 0, print `would write change file` plus the rendered changeset body, and leave no `.changeset/*.md` behind — the dry-run discipline the skill teaches agents to rely on. Without `--dry-run`, `create` writes the file and prints `wrote change file`. `monochange run change` errors while the fixture defines no `[cli.change]`, because `run` subcommands come only from `[cli.*]` config; once a `[cli.change]` wrapper is appended, it honors `--dry-run` exactly like the built-in spelling. The wrapper block is appended and the config restored inside the last check.

setupFiles..mc-cli-change-block.toml:
[cli.change]

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "interactive"
type = "boolean"
short = "i"

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "package"
type = "string_list"

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "bump"
type = "choice"
choices = ["none", "patch", "minor", "major"]
default = "patch"

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "reason"
type = "string"

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "type"
type = "string"

[[cli.change.inputs]]
name = "details"
type = "string"

[[cli.change.steps]]
type = "CreateChangeFile"
inputs = ["interactive", "package", "bump", "reason", "type", "details"]

checks.command: monochange create --package acme-core --bump minor --reason "Add streaming parser support" --dry-run; rc=$?; left=$(ls .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null); rm -rf .changeset; test $rc -eq 0 && test -z "$left"
checks.why: A dry run must exit 0, print the path it would write plus the rendered body, and leave no changeset file — a regression here is exactly the mutation agents were told cannot happen.

checks.command: monochange step create-change-file --dry-run --package acme-core --bump minor --reason "Step spelling dry run"; rc=$?; left=$(ls .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null); rm -rf .changeset; test $rc -eq 0 && test -z "$left"
checks.why: The `step create-change-file` spelling runs the same step and must obey the same dry-run discipline; the skill still teaches both spellings.

checks.command: monochange create --package acme-core --bump minor --reason "Create writes a real changeset" && test -n "$(ls .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null)" && grep -q "Create writes a real changeset" .changeset/*.md; rc=$?; rm -rf .changeset; exit $rc
checks.why: The non-dry-run spelling must actually write the changeset with the requested target, bump, and body, so the dry-run contrast is real rather than vacuous.
Run subcommands come only from `[cli.*]` config; while the fixture defines none, `change` is not even a parseable argument, and an agent relying on `run change` must see this failure.

checks.command: cp monochange.toml .mc-config-backup && cat .mc-cli-change-block.toml >> monochange.toml && monochange run change --dry-run --package acme-core --bump minor --reason "Wrapped dry run"; rc=$?; left=$(ls .changeset/*.md 2>/dev/null); mv .mc-config-backup monochange.toml; rm -rf .changeset .mc-cli-change-block.toml; test $rc -eq 0 && test -z "$left"
checks.why: Once `[cli.change]` wraps the CreateChangeFile step, the configured workflow must honor `--dry-run` identically — the wrapper is what repository CI actually invokes.
